concept_html:
Fabric notebooks run the same PySpark you wrote in Track A. The surroundings differ, and those differences break ported code (Microsoft Learn, checked September 2026).

Utilities. There is no dbutils. Fabric has NotebookUtils, formerly MSSparkUtils. The mssparkutils namespace still works but is being retired, so write notebookutils:

Databricks Fabric
dbutils.fs.ls(path) notebookutils.fs.ls(path)
dbutils.secrets.get(scope, key) notebookutils.credentials.getSecret("https://<vault>.vault.azure.net/", "name")
dbutils.notebook.run(path, timeout, args) notebookutils.notebook.run(path, timeout_seconds, arguments)
dbutils.notebook.exit(value) notebookutils.notebook.exit(value)

Secrets live in Azure Key Vault, not in Databricks secret scopes. You need Get permission on the vault. Output that prints a secret is redacted, but do not print secrets.

Child notebooks time out at 90 seconds by default. notebookutils.notebook.run(path, timeout_seconds=90, ...). A child notebook that runs for five minutes fails unless you pass a longer timeout. For several notebooks, notebookutils.notebook.runMultiple runs a DAG of them in parallel.

Default lakehouse. A notebook can attach a default lakehouse. Relative paths such as Files/landing and bare table names resolve against it. Name the lakehouse and schema in shared code (lesson C2-L1), so a changed attachment does not change what the code reads.

Inline installs. %pip install affects only the current session, and inline commands are turned off by default in pipeline runs. Put libraries in an environment instead (lesson C5-L2).

Runtime. Runtime 2.0 (Spark 4.1, Delta Lake 4.2, Python 3.13, Java 21) is GA and recommended for production. New workspaces still default to Runtime 1.3 (Spark 3.5), whose end of support has been announced. Set the runtime deliberately. It changes the Spark version your code meets.

Write `port_line(line: str) -> str` for a migration helper. It rewrites Databricks utility calls to Fabric:

- `dbutils.fs.` → `notebookutils.fs.`
- `dbutils.notebook.` → `notebookutils.notebook.`
- `mssparkutils.` → `notebookutils.`

If the line contains `dbutils.secrets.`, raise `ValueError` with a message that mentions Key Vault, because it needs a manual change. Leave other text unchanged.
exercises.prompt_html:
Write port_line(line: str) -> str for a migration helper. It rewrites Databricks utility calls to Fabric:

  • dbutils.fs. → notebookutils.fs.
  • dbutils.notebook. → notebookutils.notebook.
  • mssparkutils. → notebookutils.

If the line contains dbutils.secrets., raise ValueError with a message that mentions Key Vault, because it needs a manual change. Leave other text unchanged.
exercises.solution:
REWRITES: tuple[tuple[str, str], ...] = (
    ("dbutils.fs.", "notebookutils.fs."),
    ("dbutils.notebook.", "notebookutils.notebook."),
    ("mssparkutils.", "notebookutils."),
)


def port_line(line: str) -> str:
    """Rewrite Databricks and legacy Fabric utility calls to notebookutils.

    Raises:
        ValueError: For secret lookups, which must move to Azure Key Vault by hand.
    """
    if "dbutils.secrets." in line:
        raise ValueError("secrets need a manual change: use notebookutils.credentials.getSecret with Azure Key Vault")
    for old, new in REWRITES:
        line = line.replace(old, new)
    return line

title: From Databricks notebooks to Fabric notebooks
why_html: A team ported a Databricks orchestration notebook that called six child notebooks with mssparkutils.notebook.run(path). In development each child took under a minute. On month-end data, the largest took four minutes. Every run failed at 90 seconds with a timeout, and the error pointed at the parent notebook. Passing timeout_seconds sized to the real run time fixed it.
